newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin wants CIS summit on Afghan crisis.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin wants CIS summit on Afghan crisis.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Tuesday leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) should meet to discuss the situation in Afghanistan.
A statement from Yeltsin's press office said the Kremlin leader, who is in hospital preparing for heart surgery, had told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to contact CIS leaders.
The statement did not specify who from the 12-member group created from the ashes of the Soviet Union would be invited, nor did it set a date or venue for the proposed meeting.
It was not clear who would represent Russia.
Russia has described the latest offensive by Afghanistan's Taleban grouping, which seized the capital Kabul last Friday, as a development which could lead to a "national catastrophe".
The former Soviet republic of Tajikistan, whose pro-Moscow government opposes Afghan-based guerrillas, has said it is worried that fighting in Afghanistan could spill over into Tajik territory.

Kazakhastan, which has no border with Afghanistan, has expressed concern that fighting there could destabilise the situation in the region and asked the U.N. Security Council to meet and discuss the Afghan crisis urgently.
Russian foreign ministry spokesman Mikhail Demurin told a news briefing that senior government experts met on Tuesday to work out steps which could ensure the security of CIS members.
Demurin, reiterating earlier ministry statements, said Russia would not get involved in the crisis in any way.
"We think that it is up to the Afghans to sort out their problems and call upon others to share this vision," he said.
Soviet troops invaded Afghanistan in 1979 but Moscow withdrew the soldiers almost 10 years later after they failed to put down guerrilla resistance.
